preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 1000 for x in stdin.split()[0:2]) and 1 <= int(stdin.split()[2]) <= 10**9
preconditions.description: Input consists of three integers n (number of students), k (number of buses), and d (number of days), where 1 ≤ n, d ≤ 1000 and 1 ≤ k ≤ 10^9.
Input contains exactly three space-separated integers.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' if any(n > k**d for _ in range(1)) else True
postconditions.description: If no valid arrangement exists (i.e., n > k^d, meaning it's impossible to assign students to buses such that no two share all d days), output is exactly '-1'.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == n for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()) if stdout.strip() != '-1' else True
postconditions.description: If a valid arrangement exists, output consists of exactly d lines, each containing n space-separated integers representing bus assignments for each student on each day.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(bus) <= k for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for bus in line.split()) if stdout.strip() != '-1' else True
postconditions.description: Each bus assignment is an integer between 1 and k (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(not (all(a == b for a, b in zip(student_assignments[i], student_assignments[j])) for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n)) if stdout.strip() != '-1' else True)
postconditions.description: For any two distinct students i and j, there exists at least one day where their bus assignments differ (i.e., no two students share the same bus on all d days). Here, student_assignments is a list of lists where each sublist represents the bus assignments for a student across all d days.
